# The metric library

What a metric must say, who may add, change, remove, link and unlink one, and which metric measures a goal, for which slice.

## The rule

A **metric** is one number defined once per workspace, so every goal about it means the same thing. It has a **name**, a **unit** and a **direction** (higher or lower is better): those three are required. Everything else is optional: what it **means and how it’s calculated**, **decimals** (0 to 4; 0 when not said), its **source** and who owns that source (text), how often the source **refreshes** (live, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or not said), its **owner** (a person in the workspace: whoever added it, unless they hand it on) and **caveats**. A name is 3 to 120 characters and no other metric in use shares it, whatever the case; a unit is up to 20 characters; each text up to 2,000. Text is trimmed before it’s checked.

**Who may.** Anyone adds a metric. Only its owner or an admin changes or removes it. Only a goal’s owner or an admin says which metric measures the goal, or stops it being measured by one, whoever owns the metric.

**Measuring a goal.** A goal is measured by at most one metric, for one **slice**: a team’s number, or the whole company’s. The goal’s own target is the target in that metric (a number to move: its plan’s target; a number to keep in range: its limit); nothing is copied. A goal with dated stages has no number, so no metric measures it. The goal and the metric must have the same unit, any case. A goal aiming the other way from the metric’s better direction (planned to go up when lower is better, or kept at least a level when lower is better) is linked with a warning, since a guardrail may mean it. Linking again with the same metric and slice changes nothing; another metric or slice is a change.

**Logged, never lost.** Every change is in the change log as a metric change (adding, changing field by field, removing, restoring; linking and unlinking on the goal it measures). Removing a metric keeps its row, unlinks every goal it measured in the same save, and leaves the goals as they were. Undo straight after puts the metric and its links back; restoring it later from Recently removed brings the metric back without its old links. Unlinking keeps the link’s row too, and Undo puts it back.

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Oskar adds a metric named “Build time” with no unit or direction. | `refused: Say its unit: %, min, hours, USD, deploys… Say which way is better: higher or lower.` |
| Oskar adds “Build time”, in min, lower is better. | `Added the metric “Build time”` |
| Oskar adds “flaky TEST rate”, in %, lower is better, when “Flaky test rate” is already in the library. | `refused: There’s already a metric called Flaky test rate. Use it, or give this one a different name.` |
| Oskar changes the caveats of Flaky test rate, which Rhea owns. | `refused: Only Rhea Kapoor or an admin can change this metric.` |
| Rhea changes Flaky test rate to 2 decimals. | `Changed the metric “Flaky test rate”` |
| What measures the lead time north star (ns-lead), and its target in it. | `Lead time for changes, The whole company, target 24` |
| What measures the flaky test goal (lead-flaky, keep it at most 2%). | `Flaky test rate, CI/CD, at most 2` |
| Rhea measures her test-sharding goal (ci-shard, in %, planned 20 to 90) by Remote build cache hit rate (%, higher is better) for CI/CD. | `Measured by “Remote build cache hit rate” for CI/CD` |
| Rhea measures ci-shard (planned to go up) by Flaky test rate (lower is better). | `error: none; warning: The goal aims up, but for Flaky test rate lower is better. Check it’s meant.` |
| Grace (an admin) measures the CI pipeline time north star (ns-ci, in min) by Lead time for changes (in hours). | `refused: The goal is in min and the metric is in hours. Use the same unit for both.` |
| Grace measures the merge queue goal (lead-mq, dated stages) by Lead time for changes. | `refused: A goal with dated stages has no number, so a metric can’t measure it.` |
| Oskar measures ns-ci, which Daniel owns, by CI pipeline time on main (p90). | `refused: Only the goal’s owner or an admin can choose what measures it.` |
| Rhea measures ns-lead by Lead time for changes for the whole company, as it already is. | `nothing to save` |
| Rhea removes Lead time for changes, which measures one goal. | `Removed the metric “Lead time for changes”, unlinking 1 goal / No longer measured by “Lead time for changes”, as the metric was removed` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** Two people changing the same metric at once: the later save wins (metrics carry no version yet, unlike goals and reviews).
- **Not self-explanatory:** The words for a slice are the team’s name, or “The whole company”; the change log says “for the whole company” or “for <team>”.

### [src/domain/metrics.test.ts](../../../src/domain/metrics.test.ts)

- the demo’s library › has 13 metrics, 12 of them measuring a goal, and every link passes the rules
- the demo’s library › says what a goal is measured by, for which slice, with the goal’s own target
- the demo’s library › one metric can sit in the library measuring nothing yet
- what a metric needs › a name, a unit and a direction; everything else is optional
- what a metric needs › a name no other metric here has, any case
- what a metric needs › decimals 0 to 4, a known refresh, an owner in the workspace, text in bounds
- what a metric needs › trims what it keeps
- adding and changing a metric › anyone adds one, owns it, and it’s logged field by field
- adding and changing a metric › its owner or an admin changes it; anyone else is told who can
- adding and changing a metric › the owner can hand it on; saving it unchanged saves nothing
- linking a goal to a metric › the goal’s owner or an admin, for the company or a team
- linking a goal to a metric › the same metric and slice again changes nothing; another slice is a logged edit
- linking a goal to a metric › refuses a milestone goal, a different unit, a team that isn’t here and a removed metric
- linking a goal to a metric › warns, without refusing, when the goal aims the other way from the metric
- linking a goal to a metric › unlinking keeps the row, logs it, and Undo puts it back
- removing a metric › its owner or an admin; it unlinks its goals, and Undo brings both back
- removing a metric › is on Recently removed, and restoring brings the metric back without its old links
- removing a metric › can’t come back under a name another metric took since
- one form, one save › mergeCommits puts a goal’s save and its link together, in order
